title: High average human development does not settle the question of who can exercise new choices
source_unit: UNDP Human Development Reports country-level composite index and ranking for the United States
geography: United States; international comparison across 193 countries and territories

observations.method: UNDP Human Development Reports country-insights summary; HDI combines normalized life expectancy, education, and gross national income per capita dimensions using a geometric mean.
observations.uncertainty: The HDI is an average composite, uses data available to the Human Development Report Office, and does not capture within-country inequality, poverty, human security, empowerment, institutional trust, or who can exercise a capability.
observations.subgroup: United States aggregate; no household, worker, race, gender, age, place, or income subgroup.
observations.counterinterpretation: An improving country average can coexist with unequal gains, worsening outcomes for particular groups, or reduced practical choice in housing, care, work, health, or digital systems.

observations.period: 2023; United States international position in the 2025 Human Development Report

denominator.unit: countries and territories in the UNDP comparison

observations.method: UNDP country-insights comparison using the 2025 Human Development Report data update; rank is a cross-country ordering of the composite index.
observations.uncertainty: Rank differences may be small and not statistically meaningful at fine decimal places; the report warns that editions and revisions are not automatically comparable without the consistent trend table. Rank is not a measure of social cohesion, state capacity, or practical agency.
observations.subgroup: United States country aggregate compared with all listed countries and territories.
observations.counterinterpretation: A high rank can conceal distributional gaps and does not imply that AI, income, health, education, or institutional power are equally accessible within the United States.

related_sources.claim: UNDP’s 2025 Global Survey on AI and Human Development is a potential perception-and-choice layer for the broader human-development comparison.
UNDP provides technical notes and consistent trend tables needed before comparing index movement across editions.

boundary: This is a bounded UNDP human-development context record. It establishes a high US average HDI and its reported long-run change, not equal capability, household welfare, AI access, worker control, political trust, or geopolitical power. Composite-country averages remain a comparison frame for the US-centered program, not a substitute for subgroup and same-unit evidence.
